apbio.current: AP Biology Chapter 13, meiosis and sexual life cycles. The Fri 11/13 quiz covers meiosis plus Mendelian genetics and Hardy-Weinberg; the teacher starred the Ch 13 slides in class, and Carter's own priority list names karyotype, homologous chromosomes, sex chromosomes and autosomes as sure items.
focus: gamete = sperm or egg, produced by meiosis, the only haploid cells in animals; fertilization restores 2n = 46 in the zygote
karyotype reading: 23 pairs, 22 autosome pairs plus one sex pair, XX vs XY, homologous pairs matched by length and shape
crossing over in prophase I: synapsis, chiasmata, recombinant chromosomes, more genetic variation
independent assortment at metaphase I and the 2^n gamete-combination formula (2^23 is about 8.4 million in humans)
anaphase I separates homologous chromosomes while sister chromatids stay attached; anaphase II separates sister chromatids
one S phase, two divisions, no replication between meiosis I and II; four haploid daughter cells, each genetically distinct
the three sources of genetic variation: independent assortment, crossing over, random fertilization
nondisjunction: all four gametes abnormal means meiosis I failed, two of four abnormal means meiosis II failed; trisomy vs monosomy
Mendelian testcross logic: no recessive offspring means homozygous dominant, a 1:1 ratio means heterozygous
Hardy-Weinberg one direction: the recessive phenotype count is q^2, then q, p = 1 - q, and heterozygotes = 2pq
her question style: name the phase, give the chromosome and chromatid count, predict the consequence of a defect
